**Context Note: Open Door Literacy Annual Gala Planning (2024)**

The 2024 annual gala is being planned as a high-impact, mission-centered event with a focus on dignity, authenticity, and sustainable donor engagement. The event will be held in four months, with 220 guests, and is the organization’s largest annual fundraising opportunity.

**Theme:**  
The 1920s speakeasy evening with a live jazz trio has been selected as the official theme. This was chosen over a casino night (exclusionary, not aligned with mission) and a trivia-night format (lacks emotional resonance). The theme is titled *“The Roaring Twenties: A Night of Jazz, Stories, and Quiet Courage”* — a narrative that reflects the quiet agency and resilience of literacy learners.

**Event Structure & Flow:**  
- The program is designed to be 120 minutes, with a strong opening, emotional storytelling, and a live auction segment.  
- The live auction will occur *after* a high-impact student story is shared — not at the start — to build momentum and emotional investment.  
- The emcee will be a trusted staff member (not a celebrity), chosen for their deep connection to the mission and ability to speak with warmth and rhythm.  
- The auctioneer’s license (AU-77031) is on file and will be provided upon request.

**Donor Outreach:**  
- 75 lapsed donors who gave $500+ in the past but not in three years are being reactivated via personal calls.  
- Aisha is leading outreach; 4 calls per week are recommended to maintain sustainability and emotional depth.  
- All messaging must lead with dignity — no pity narratives, no tragic framing. Learners are portrayed as capable adults choosing to grow.

**Fundraising & Systems:**  
- The $1,000–$5,000 matching pledge from board member Elaine will be announced during the live auction, after a student story.  
- Givly and similar text-to-give platforms are rejected due to 11% fees and poor reconciliation.  
- Stripe will be used for all day-of donations — transparent, low-fee, and fully reconcilable.  
- The monthly giving program, **Orchard**, is now a standalone initiative (not the community orchard volunteer project). It will have a dedicated, simple, and mission-driven page on the Open Door Literacy website.

**Stewardship & Retention:**  
- Post-event stewardship will begin within 48 hours.  
- All donors who gave $500+ will receive a handwritten-style note within 3 days, referencing a personal story from the night.  
- The goal is to turn one-time donors into year-round supporters by reinforcing belonging, not transaction.

**Rules of Engagement:**  
- No golf tournaments — rejected as exclusionary and misaligned with mission.  
- No jargon: “the match” refers only to Elaine’s $1,000–$5,000 matching pledge. “Orchard” refers only to the monthly giving program.  
- No mass outreach to local businesses — only targeted, mission-aligned partnerships.

**Open Threads:**  
- Finalize the live auction script and timing.  
- Design the Orchard website page (simple, story-driven, with a $50/month option).  
- Confirm the 4-call/week schedule for Aisha’s outreach.  
- Finalize decor budget for the 1920s speakeasy theme (target: $12,000–$15,000).  
- Confirm the 120-minute program timeline with the emcee.

**Decisions Made:**  
- 1920s speakeasy theme (not casino or trivia).  
- Live auction after a student story (not at start).  
- Stripe for donations (not Givly).  
- Orchard has a website page (not just a table card).  
- No celebrity emcee (staff-led).  
- No golf, no pity, no jargon.

**Context Note: Open Door Literacy Annual Gala Planning (2024)**

The annual gala is scheduled for four months out, with 220 guests, and is the organization’s largest revenue-generating event of the year. The planning process has been guided by a clear mission-centered philosophy: every decision must reflect dignity, inclusion, and authenticity — not jargon, exclusion, or transactional language.

**Theme:** The 1920s speakeasy evening with a live jazz trio has been finalized. This theme was chosen over a casino night (exclusionary, not aligned with mission) and a trivia-night format (lacked emotional resonance). The theme is titled *“The Roaring Twenties: A Night of Jazz, Stories, and Quiet Courage”* — a narrative that mirrors the journey of literacy learners as capable, courageous adults choosing to grow.

**Emcee:** A celebrity emcee was ruled out due to cost ($8,500 + travel) and lack of alignment with mission. Instead, a trusted staff member or volunteer with storytelling experience will serve as emcee — chosen for authenticity, connection to learners, and ability to embody the theme’s tone.

**Donor Outreach:** A targeted reactivation campaign has been launched for 75 lapsed donors who previously gave $500 or more. These are not to be contacted via mass email. Instead, each will receive a personalized, story-driven call or message focused on emotional connection, not fundraising. The goal is 20–30 reactivated donors.

**Auction:** Gift baskets have been ruled out as ineffective and low-impact. The silent auction will feature experiential and story-based items (e.g., “One-Minute Story” with a student, “Time in the Classroom” with a teacher, “Book to Life” with a real learner). A live auction will be held during the event, but only after a high-emotion story bid — to maximize energy and connection.

**Matching Gift:** Board member Elaine’s dollar-for-dollar matching pledge (up to a threshold) will be announced during the live auction — not in a cold list, but as a moment of collective momentum, following a powerful story.

**Orchard:** The monthly-giving program is named *Orchard*. It is not the community orchard volunteer project. *Orchard* refers to recurring gifts ($50/month, $100/month) that support literacy. A dedicated, simple, and beautiful page on the Open Door Literacy website will be launched before the gala — not just a signup card.

**Payments:** Givly and similar text-to-give platforms have been ruled out due to 11% fees and 3-day reconciliation. A Stripe-based system will be used for all day-of donations — transparent, low-fee, and fully reconcilable.

**Compliance:** The auctioneer’s license (AU-77031) has been verified and filed — no longer a risk.

**Stewardship:** Post-gala stewardship will not be transactional. Donors will receive a handwritten-style note from a staff member, a “Letter from the Learner,” and an invitation to join the “Roaring Twenties Circle” — a private group for year-round engagement.

**Open Threads:**  
- Finalizing the 4-call-per-week schedule for Aisha’s outreach (100 calls over 6 weeks).  
- Designing the Orchard website page (simple, story-driven, no jargon).  
- Finalizing the live auction script and timing (after a student story).  
- Confirming the emcee’s name and training.

**Constraints & Preferences:**  
- No golf tournaments (exclusionary, not aligned with mission).  
- No pity narratives or tragic framing of learners.  
- No jargon: “match” = Elaine’s pledge; “Orchard” = monthly giving.  
- No mass outreach, no cold calls, no generic thank-yous.

**Ruled Out:**  
- Celebrity emcees (cost, misalignment).  
- Givly and similar platforms (fees, poor reconciliation).  
- Gift baskets (low bid value, generic).  
- Mass email outreach (lacks personal connection).  
- “Thank you” emails without stories or belonging.
